manuscripts.title: A torsion-free hyperbolic group that is not residually finite

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: There exists a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite.

candidates.label: Corollary 1.2
candidates.name: Finite-dimensional linear obstruction
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.2 (Finite-dimensional linear obstruction).
candidates.statement: Let G be the finitely generated torsion-free word-hyperbolic group constructed in Theorem 1.1. For every commutative field K, every integer n ≥ 1, and every homomorphism ρ : G → GLn(K), Rf (G) ⊆ ker ρ. Consequently, one fixed nonidentity element of G is killed by all these representations, simultane- ously over all such fields and dimensions. In particular, G is not linear over any commutative field.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.1
candidates.name: Triangle complex criterion
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.1 (Triangle complex criterion).
candidates.statement: Let K be a connected finite Euclidean triangle complex. Suppose there is η > 0 such that every nonempty cyclically reduced closed edge walk in each vertex link has angular length at least 2π + η. Then π1(K) is torsion-free and word-hyperbolic. Moreover, a nonempty closed edge path in K is not nullhomotopic if every cyclic turn has link distance at least π. Here a turn compares the direction back along the arriving edge with the direction of the departing edge.

candidates.name: Closed paths

candidates.heading: Proposition 4.3 (Transfer to the Cayley graph).

If π1Y is Baumslag– Solitar-free, then, for every connected subgraph S ⊆ Γ with λ(S1) ⊈ S, the map π1S −→ π1Y is injective and its image is quasiconvex.

candidates.label: Corollary 2.7
candidates.heading: Corollary 2.7.
candidates.statement: Let P be a finitely generated free group and E ≤ P a strongly inert subgroup. If g ∈ P \ E, then E ∩ gEg−1 is trivial or cyclic.

candidates.label: Theorem 3.1
candidates.name: Restricted combination theorem
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.1 (Restricted combination theorem).
candidates.statement: Let H be a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group, let A, B ≤ H be finitely generated free quasiconvex subgroups, and let ϕ: A → B be an isomorphism. Set G = ⟨H, t | tat−1 = ϕ(a) (a ∈ A)⟩, P = A, I = A ∩ B, J = t−1 It ≤ P. Assume the following two conditions. (i) For M, N ∈ {A, B} and g ∈ H, the intersection M ∩gNg−1 is at most cyclic unless g ∈ MN. (ii) The groups I, J are finitely generated, and each E ∈ {I, J} satisfies X SpE∈S\P/E r̄(E ∩ p−1 Sp) ≤ r̄(S) for every finitely generated S ≤ P. (3.1) 8 If G contains no subgroup isomorphic to BS(m, n) for any nonzero integers m, n, then G is word-hyperbolic.

candidates.label: Theorem 3.5
candidates.name: Algebraic annular flaring
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.5 (Algebraic annular flaring).
candidates.statement: Let H be word-hyperbolic, let A, B ≤ H be finitely generated, and let ϕ : A → B be an isomorphism such that both attaching maps A → H are quasi-isometric embeddings. Set G = ⟨H, t | tat−1 = ϕ(a), a ∈ A⟩. Then G is word-hyperbolic if there exist λ > 1 and an integer m ≥ 1 such that, for every ρ > 0, there is h(ρ) for which every essential algebraic annulus as defined above, with 2m + 1 rows, width at most ρ, and girth at least h(ρ), is λ-hyperbolic.
candidates.cited_by: This is the algebraic formulation of the Bestvina–Feighn combination theorem in [1, Theo- rem 1.2]; we use its explicit annular statement in [8, Definitions 4.1–4.4 and Theorem 4.5].
references: [1] Mladen Bestvina and Mark Feighn. Addendum and correction to “a combination theo- rem for negatively curved groups”. Journal of Differential Geometry, 43(4):783–788, 1996. doi:10.4310/jdg/1214458531.

[8] Ilya Kapovich. A non-quasiconvexity embedding theorem for hyperbolic groups. Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society, 127(3):461–486, 1999. Citations refer to arXiv:math/9704203v1, 11 April 1997; doi:10.1017/S0305004199003862.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.12
candidates.name: The current trajectory forced by nonflaring
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.12 (The current trajectory forced by nonflaring).
candidates.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theo- rem 3.1, if G is not hyperbolic, there exist currents µs ∈ Curr(P) for s ∈ Z, signs ϵs ∈ {+, −}, and transition types τs with signs (ϵs, ϵs+1), such that (i) ∥µ0∥ = 1, every µs is nonzero, and sups∈Z ∥µs∥ < ∞; (ii) for every s there is a current νs ∈ Curr(Kτs ) with µs = (θτs,0)∗νs, µs+1 = (θτs,1)∗νs; (iii) all types are essential: any reversing type uses a double coset outside the common side subgroup. The constants in (3.14) apply to this trajectory. In particular, ∥µs∥ ≥ C−|s| for all s.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.4
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.4.
candidates.statement: Let (µs)s∈Z be a bounded sequence of nonzero P-currents with transition currents and compatible essential types as in Proposition 3.12. If G is Baumslag–Solitar free, every µs is atomless.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.5
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.5.
candidates.statement: Under the assumptions of Proposition 4.4, there exist a nonzero current ν on I and a nonzero atomless current µ on P such that i∗ν = j∗ν = µ. (4.1) In particular, if the restricted HNN extension is not hyperbolic, Proposition 3.12 supplies such a stationary current.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.7
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.7.
candidates.statement: There is a translation- and flip-invariant conull Borel set U ⊂ Ω with the following properties. (i) Every line of U has two irrational endpoints and is carried by a unique I coset and a unique J coset. (ii) On lines carried by pΛI, translate by p−1 and apply the boundary isomorphism from I to J. This forward transfer, and the analogous backward transfer from qΛJ, preserve µ on their domains. (iii) Every defined transfer, its inverse, and every output frame translation take lines of U to lines of U. Consequently all successive forward and backward transfers exist on U. Measure preservation in (ii) holds on the full Borel domain of lines with irrational endpoints, not only after restriction to U.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.8
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.8.
candidates.statement: Every line L ∈ U determines an actual aligned bilateral path of positively traversed edges · · · , E−1, E0 = e, E1, · · · in T , with transferred lines in its successive edge frames. The following properties hold. (i) The path is independent of coset representatives and of compatible changes of frames and line coordinates. (ii) For every finite window containing E0, its stabilizer K ≤ P is finitely generated and noncyclic, and the endpoints of L lie in ΛK. (iii) Two distinct actual aligned windows of the same shape about e have at most cyclic common stabilizer. In particular, an irrational point can belong to the limit sets of at most one such window stabilizer. (iv) If an aligned one-sided window joins e to he, its stabilizer is S = P ∩ hPh−1. The boundary map of S −→ h−1 Sh, x 7−→ h−1 xh, implements its line transfer. On the irrational-endpoint domain it preserves µ; it takes its domain in U into U. In (iii), a shape specifies the numbers of edges before and after the central edge, all traversed positively.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.5
candidates.name: Finite cofinal carriers
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.5 (Finite cofinal carriers).
candidates.statement: The noncyclic component subgroup classes of Γsm belong to C and form a finite cofinal subset: every [Q] ∈ C is contained, up to P-conjugacy, in one of them. In particular C has only finitely many maximal elements, and they are exactly the maximal members of this finite family.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.6
candidates.name: Atoroidal return
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.6 (Atoroidal return).
candidates.statement: The map F is an order-preserving bijection with order- preserving inverse. It permutes the finite set of maximal classes of C. For every representative M of such a class, there are an integer p ≥ 1 and an element v ∈ G of height p such that v−1 Mv = M. The automorphism α : M → M, α(m) = v−1mv, is atoroidal: no nontrivial conjugacy class in M is periodic under α.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.8
candidates.name: Zero mass on a maximal carrier
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.8 (Zero mass on a maximal carrier).
candidates.statement: For every maximal carrier M supplied by Proposition 5.5, µ(∂2 ΛM) = 0. The same holds for every P-translate of this line set.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.4
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.4.
candidates.statement: If Ω contains a line carried, up to translation, by a maximal noncyclic carrier M, then Ω contains a periodic line.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.8
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.8.
candidates.statement: The support Ω contains no periodic line.

candidates.label: Corollary 6.9
candidates.heading: Corollary 6.9.
candidates.statement: The following assertions hold for the closed support Ω. 1. No line of Ω is carried by the small subgraph. There is an integer B0 such that every segment of a lift of an Ω-line to any of the selected subsequence cores Γn, if contained entirely in the small subgraph, has length at most B0. 40 2. Every endpoint of every line of Ω is irrational. 3. Every line of Ω lifts to each centered core union Γn and has a unique compatible bilateral trajectory. On each fixed window, the partial boundary transfer takes every support line in its domain to a line of Ω.

candidates.label: Proposition 8.4
candidates.heading: Proposition 8.4.
candidates.statement: Let Γ be a finite connected graph, and let λ: S1 → Γ be a nontrivial immersed circuit representing a non-power in π1Γ. If π1(Γ ∪λ D2) is BS-free, then it is word-hyperbolic.

candidates.label: Corollary 9.1
candidates.heading: Corollary 9.1.
candidates.statement: Let X be finite, let r ∈ F(X), and suppose that G = F(X)/⟨⟨r⟩⟩ contains no subgroup isomorphic to BS(m, n) for any nonzero integers m, n. There are a finite-index subgroup H ≤ G, an integer d ≥ 0, an automorphism α of the rank-d free group Fd, and an embedding H ,→ Fd ⋊α Z. Consequently the same H fits into an exact sequence 1 −→ K −→ H −→ Q −→ 1, K free, Q ≤ Z. Thus G is virtually free-by-cyclic, with the rank of K allowed to be infinite and Q allowed to be trivial.

manuscripts.title: Virtual compact specialness of hyperbolic one-relator groups

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Let X be finite, let r ∈ F(X), and suppose that G = F(X)/⟨⟨r⟩⟩ is word-hyperbolic. Then G is virtually compact special. More precisely, there are a finite- index subgroup H ≤ G, a finite connected nonpositively curved cube complex C, and a finite simplicial graph Λ such that π1(C) ∼ = H and C −→ SΛ is a cubical local isometry to the Salvetti complex of the right-angled Artin group defined by Λ.

candidates.label: Theorem 1.2
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.2.
candidates.statement: Let F be a finitely generated free group and let ϕ : F → F be injective. If its ascending mapping torus F∗ϕ = ⟨F, t | t−1 ft = ϕ(f), f ∈ F⟩ 2 is word-hyperbolic, then it is virtually compact special.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.1
candidates.name: Cubulation and quasiconvex hierarchies
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.1 (Cubulation and quasiconvex hierarchies).
candidates.statement: 1. A word-hyperbolic group acting properly and cocompactly on a CAT(0) cube complex is virtually compact special. 2. A hyperbolic group with a finite graph-of-groups decomposition whose edge groups are quasiconvex in the ambient group and whose vertex groups are hyperbolic VCS is VCS. The same applies to a finite hierarchy of such decompositions. 3. A compact special cube complex admits a cubical local isometry to a Salvetti complex. Its defining graph can be taken finite.
candidates.cited_by: These are the virtual special theorem [2, Theorem 1.1], the quasiconvex hierarchy theorem [66, Theorem 13.1], and the special-complex characterization [28, Proposition 3.10 and Theorem 4.2], respectively.
references: [2] I. Agol, The virtual Haken conjecture, with an appendix by I. Agol, D. Groves, and J. Manning, Documenta Mathematica 18 (2013), 1045–1087. doi:10.4171/DM/421. arXiv:1204.2810.
[66] D. T. Wise, The Structure of Groups with a Quasiconvex Hierarchy, Annals of Mathematics Studies, vol. 209, Princeton University Press, Princeton, NJ, 2021. doi:10.1515/9780691213507.

[28] F. Haglund and D. T. Wise, Special cube complexes, Geometric and Functional Anal- ysis 17 (2008), no. 5, 1551–1620. doi:10.1007/s00039-007-0629-4. Corrected author version, used for theorem locators: https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/ ~frederic.haglund/special(corrected).pdf.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.2
candidates.name: Reduction
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.2 (Reduction).
candidates.statement: To prove Theorem 1.1, it suffices to prove that every torsion- free hyperbolic primitive extension group in the two forms of [40, Section 5] is VCS.

candidates.label: Theorem 3.1
candidates.name: Filling criterion
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.1 (Filling criterion).
candidates.statement: Let G∗ be a torsion-free hyperbolic group satisfying the following conditions. (i) G∗ is locally indicable, coherent, of type F, and has integral cohomological dimension at most two. (ii) G∗ has a division ring D(G∗) satisfying the subgroup-field hypotheses, and the chains of a finite classifying space become acyclic over D(G∗). (iii) There is a finite malnormal family {Dj} of quasiconvex hyperbolic virtually compact special subgroups such that arbitrarily deep peripheral fillings G∗ −→ Q∗ are hyperbolic and virtually compact special, and their inherited peripheral images are hyperbolic and virtually compact special. In (iii), arbitrarily deep means that the peripheral kernels can avoid any prescribed finite subset of S j(Dj \ {1}); the inherited peripheral structure is the one furnished by relative Dehn filling. Then a finite-index subgroup of G∗ is an extension of a finite-rank free group by Z. Consequently G∗ is virtually compact special.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.3
candidates.name: Selective-cover quotient
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.3 (Selective-cover quotient).
candidates.statement: Choose (3.2) sufficiently deep. Let Hgiven be a finite-index preimage in G∗, and let B ⊂ A be finite. There is a further finite-index preimage H ≤ Hgiven, normal in Hgiven, such that, on retaining all factors indexed by the H-translates of B and killing the other factors, the group P = H/K− (3.4) is hyperbolic and virtually compact special. The natural map to P is injective on ∗a∈BRa.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.11
candidates.name: Progressive characters
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.11 (Progressive characters).
candidates.statement: Let J be finitely generated with the subgroup-field hypotheses, and let K ◁ J satisfy the selective realization property of Definition 3.7. Every finite family of rational expressions over QJ can, after restriction of scalars to a finite-index subgroup F, be realized compatibly in the ordinary Novikov rings for both signs of a single real character of F. In particular, if a finite complex of finitely generated free QJ-modules is acyclic over D(J), then its restriction is acyclic over both these Novikov rings. If its degree-zero ordinary homology is nonzero, the character is nonzero.

candidates.label: Corollary 3.12
candidates.name: Open Novikov regions for RFRS groups
candidates.heading: Corollary 3.12 (Open Novikov regions for RFRS groups).
candidates.statement: Let J be virtually RFRS with the subgroup-field hypotheses. A finite family of bounded complexes of finitely generated free QJ-modules, with polynomial differential matrices and acyclic extension to D(J), admits simultaneous ordinary Novikov contractions, after passage to a finite-index subgroup F, on a nonempty antipodally invariant open subset of Hom(F, R). Here the character space has the topology of pointwise convergence. This property can be imposed after any prescribed further finite-index restriction.

candidates.label: Theorem 4.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 4.1.
candidates.statement: Let F be a free group of finite rank and let ϕ : F → F be injective. If Jϕ is word-hyperbolic, then Jϕ is virtually compact special.

candidates.label: Corollary 4.10
candidates.heading: Corollary 4.10.
candidates.statement: Let F be a free group of finite rank and let ϕ : F → F be injective. If Jϕ is word-hyperbolic, it has a finite-index subgroup H fitting into an exact sequence 1 −→ Fd −→ H −→ Z −→ 1 for some finite d ≥ 0, where Fd is the rank-d free group. Thus H ∼ = Fd ⋊α Z for an automorphism α of Fd.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.6
candidates.name: Restriction to row orbits
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.6 (Restriction to row orbits).
candidates.statement: For U ≤ L and an actual level L , inclusion and the above coefficient transport give an injection M ξ∈U\L H1(U ∩ Xξ; DU ) −→ H1(U; DU ). (5.4) For U in a vertex row, the analogous sum over one incident slot injects. The same assertions hold for coarse rows. The assertions hold in the induced chain modules before passing to an overfield.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.7
candidates.name: Path inertia
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.7 (Path inertia).
candidates.statement: In T and T0, every path with noncyclic pointwise stabilizer is monotone. For each fixed monotone shape in a fixed absolute level range, the first homologies of its stabilizers, indexed modulo L, inject jointly into H1(L; DL). A path containing an edge has finitely generated free stabilizer, and a fixed finite shape has finitely many G-orbits with nontrivial stabilizer, or finitely many L-orbits when its absolute level range is fixed. In particular X γ mod L max{rk Stab(γ) − 1, 0} ≤ k − 1. (5.5) The same joint-injection statement holds for continuations of any fixed additional shape inside any subgroup U of a current path stabilizer, with the intersection summands indexed by U- orbits. It holds after restriction of the actual induced matrices and double-coset decompositions, not just as a numerical inequality.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.11
candidates.name: Period rule
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.11 (Period rule).
candidates.statement: Suppose A ≤ G, h(A) ̸= 0, and S = A ∩ L, 0 < β(S) < ∞. 40 At every actual level L , inclusion induces an isomorphism M ξ∈S\L H1(S ∩ Xξ; DS) −→ H1(S; DS). Both incident edge-level maps to a vertex level are isomorphisms. Every level sum therefore has dimension qX = β(S). The convex hull Y of the rows with noncyclic S ∩ Xξ contains no edge with trivial S-stabilizer. If A is also finitely generated, then A\Y is finite and A is quasiconvex in G.

candidates.label: Theorem 6.1
candidates.name: Support and coset descent
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.1 (Support and coset descent).
candidates.statement: The following assertions hold. (i) If S ∩ T = ∅, then V(S) ∩ V(T) = 0. (ii) There is a Q-linear map F : DJ −→ QJ with F(1) = δ1, commuting with every right group translation, such that v ∈ V(S) implies supp F(v) ⊆ S. (iii) Let A, B ≤ J and C = A ∩ B. If At ∩ Bs is empty, then DAt ∩ DBs = 0. Otherwise, for any x ∈ At ∩ Bs, DAt ∩ DBs = DCx. (6.2) If, in addition, C is separable in both A and B, then   X g∈J DAg   ∩   X g∈J DBg   = X g∈J DCg, (6.3) 42 where each sum denotes its algebraic, finite-support span.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.4
candidates.name: Affiliated positive mean
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.4 (Affiliated positive mean).
candidates.statement: Let Xn, n ∈ Z, be positive affiliated units in a finite von Neumann algebra. Suppose that both {Xn} and {X−1 n } are tight. There is a unique positive affiliated unit P satisfying MnF(P, Xn) = 1 2 1. (7.7) The construction is covariant under congruence by affiliated invertible operators, including affiliated invertible maps between corners with their restricted traces.

candidates.label: Corollary 8.5
candidates.name: Persistence of a rational line
candidates.heading: Corollary 8.5 (Persistence of a rational line).
candidates.statement: Suppose a bilateral trajectory carries, in R0, the whole axis of a loxodromic element c ∈ H0 through every finite subwindow containing position zero. Some nonzero power of c fixes the entire trajectory pointwise.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.8
candidates.name: The component trees
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.8 (The component trees).
candidates.statement: Every component of the actual switch graph is a tree. For a nonisolated component with stabilizer A and S = A ∩ L, there is an integer r ≥ 2 such that S is a nested union of rank-r free groups and dimDL H1(S; DL) = r − 1. These approximants and S have injective ambient first-homology maps. Moreover A is finitely generated, quasiconvex, virtually compact special, and field-acyclic.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.9
candidates.name: Capture by periodic quasiconvex groups
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.9 (Capture by periodic quasiconvex groups).
candidates.statement: Unless G is already virtually compact special by the acylindrical case, there is an invariant system of actual objects, finite modulo G, with full stabilizers A and kernels S = A ∩ L, having these properties: (i) h(A) ̸= 0; each A is quasiconvex, virtually compact special, and field-acyclic. (ii) Each S is a nested union of finite-rank free approximants of one constant rank at least two. Its field first-homology dimension is positive and finite, and its ambient homology detects every noncyclic subgroup. (iii) For representatives of the actual object orbits under L, the maps M H1(S; DL) −→ H1(L; DL) are jointly injective. Distinct actual object stabilizers intersect in at most cyclic groups. (iv) There is a uniform length such that the pointwise stabilizer of every longer noncyclically stabilized actual path, in T0 or in the refined tree T, is wholly contained in one of these kernels S.

candidates.label: Proposition 10.5
candidates.name: Joint injection after a cyclic join
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.5 (Joint injection after a cyclic join).
candidates.statement: For the new component system the map M i∈L\D′ H1(S′ i; DL) −→ H1(L; DL) is injective. Consequently a cyclic-join round preserves admissibility and does not decrease the budget. A round containing a positive-height cyclic join increases the budget by at least one.

candidates.label: Proposition 10.6
candidates.name: Finite strict closure
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.6 (Finite strict closure).
candidates.statement: Iterating cyclic joins stops after finitely many rounds. The final system is admissible and strictly malnormal: stabilizers of distinct objects have trivial intersection. Each is the full stabilizer of its object. For each final object d, the union of all actual rows x with Xx ∩ Sd ̸= 1 is a connected subtree Zd with finite Dd-quotient, where Dd is its object stabilizer and Sd = Dd ∩ L.

candidates.label: Proposition 11.6
candidates.name: Folded slot structure and restriction
candidates.heading: Proposition 11.6 (Folded slot structure and restriction).
candidates.statement: Fix a folded vertex v and one slot of incident folded edges f. Let Kf be the image of the endpoint map Γf → Γv. Then Kf is a Yf -cocompact subtree, every object vertex d of Γv occurs in exactly one such Kf with its full stabilizer, and any absent incidence has at most cyclic stabilizer. For each H ≤ Yv the 82 natural map M f mod H H1(H ∩ Yf ; DL) −→ H1(H; DL) (11.1) is injective.

candidates.label: Corollary 11.7
candidates.name: Strict folded tree
candidates.heading: Corollary 11.7 (Strict folded tree).
candidates.statement: The quotient b T is a tree with one L-orbit at each level, and every Zd maps onto a monotone line ℓd. Its row groups and slot maps have the conclusions of Lemmas 11.4 and 11.5 and Proposition 11.6. Stabilizers of finite monotone paths in any fixed height range inject jointly on first field homology into L, over path-orbit representatives.

candidates.label: Proposition 12.3
candidates.name: The tail free-product decomposition
candidates.heading: Proposition 12.3 (The tail free-product decomposition).
candidates.statement: Let K be the pointwise stabilizer of a positive ray contained in an old line, starting at an actual free-edge level w. An object vertex of Γw is called full if its line contains that entire tail. There are finitely many K-orbits 85 of full vertices. With representatives d1, . . . , dm, one has K ∼ =  ∗m j=1Sdj  ∗ Fr, r < ∞. (12.1) The displayed embeddings of full factors are their actual subgroup embeddings, up to the usual independent choices of conjugating basepoint paths.

candidates.label: Proposition 12.5
candidates.name: Quasiconvex and virtually compact special end groups
candidates.heading: Proposition 12.5 (Quasiconvex and virtually compact special end groups).
candidates.statement: Each end stabilizer Aξ is finitely generated, quasiconvex in G, field-acyclic, and virtually compact special. It is torsion-free, locally indicable, coherent, of type F, and of cohomological dimension at most two.

candidates.label: Proposition 12.6
candidates.name: Strict growth at a shared end
candidates.heading: Proposition 12.6 (Strict growth at a shared end).
candidates.statement: Replacing the objects by distinct end stabilizers preserves all admissibility conditions. If some two distinct old lines share an end in the chosen orientation, this replacement strictly increases the budget. Subsequent cyclic closure does not decrease it.

candidates.label: Theorem 12.7
candidates.name: Terminal periodic system
candidates.heading: Theorem 12.7 (Terminal periodic system).
candidates.statement: Starting with the system of Proposition 9.9, finitely many cyclic-closure and end-enlargement rounds produce an admissible strict malnor- mal quasiconvex virtually compact special system {Dd}, with Sd = Dd ∩ L, and a folded tree b T having all the conclusions of Corollary 11.7. The associated monotone lines ℓd of distinct objects share no end. Actual long noncyclic path stabilizers remain captured, the kernels still detect all noncyclic subgroups, and their joint homology budget is at most k − 1.

candidates.label: Corollary 13.8
candidates.name: Unfilled nonparabolic double cosets
candidates.heading: Corollary 13.8 (Unfilled nonparabolic double cosets).
candidates.statement: For fixed exact relative embeddings of B, C in a row J, the double cosets BgC having nonparabolic intersection B ∩ gCg−1 have representatives in a fixed finite subset of J.

candidates.label: Proposition 14.1
candidates.name: Simultaneous relative factors
candidates.heading: Proposition 14.1 (Simultaneous relative factors).
candidates.statement: For a sufficiently long monotone folded path W, its pointwise stabilizer H has a finite relative free-product decomposition H =  ∗m j=1(H ∩ Sdj )  ∗ Fr. The factors represent exactly the nontrivial peripheral intersections, up to H-conjugacy. Vertices of the corresponding relative Bass–Serre tree that have nontrivial stabilizer carry injective, equivariant labels by actual objects d. The trivial vertices can be chosen of finite valence.

candidates.label: Proposition 14.2
candidates.name: Terminal path bound
candidates.heading: Proposition 14.2 (Terminal path bound).
candidates.statement: There is a length n0 such that every segment of b T of length at least n0 has trivial, cyclic, or parabolic pointwise stabilizer. Moreover there is a uniform bound on the length of a segment fixed by any nontrivial height-zero element lying outside all the Sd.

candidates.label: Corollary 14.3
candidates.name: The additional root cyclic
candidates.heading: Corollary 14.3 (The additional root cyclic).
candidates.statement: In the root case in which no power of the root cyclic group is claimed by the object system, its maximal cyclic overgroup may be added to the peripheral family. Its nontrivial incidences have finite orbit lists, and the relative embeddings and finite-path conclusions continue to hold with the enlarged induced systems.

candidates.label: Corollary 14.7
candidates.name: Finite double-coset representatives
candidates.heading: Corollary 14.7 (Finite double-coset representatives).
candidates.statement: For fixed original exact relative em- beddings of B, C in a row, every double coset in a sufficiently long filling whose intersection contains an infinite-order loxodromic element has a representative in the image of a fixed finite original list. The list is independent of the double coset and of the filling.

candidates.label: Proposition 14.8
candidates.name: Exact intersection transfer
candidates.heading: Proposition 14.8 (Exact intersection transfer).
candidates.statement: Fix exact relative embeddings B, C ,→ J with the full-or-cyclic induced peripheral systems described above, and fix g ∈ J. There are finitely many compatibility requests of Definition 14.4, determined in the original groups, such that every sufficiently long filling satisfying them has B̄ ∩ ḡC̄ḡ−1 = B ∩ gCg−1. The notation B̄, C̄ denotes the embedded standalone fillings given by Lemma 14.5.

candidates.label: Theorem 14.9
candidates.name: Finite-path transfer
candidates.heading: Theorem 14.9 (Finite-path transfer).
candidates.statement: Fix an integer n. Under the terminal row hypotheses, there is a finite set of original compatibility requests such that every sufficiently long compatible filling has the following properties. (i) The induced row fillings and edge fillings form the quotient graph of groups for Ḡ. (ii) Every reduced path of length at most n downstairs with infinite stabilizer lifts, after the permitted changes of Bass–Serre representatives, to an actual reduced path upstairs. Its stabilizer is exactly the image of the actual path stabilizer. (iii) Taking n at least the terminal path bound, the resulting Bass–Serre action is acylindrical: sufficiently long segment stabilizers are finite of uniformly bounded order. Each filled row is hyperbolic and each edge map is quasi-isometric. Here the ambient filled group is hyperbolic by sufficiently long filling of the original relatively hyperbolic pair: the periodic peripheral reductions are finite-by-cyclic and hence hyperbolic, and the additional cyclic reductions are finite. The conclusion about ambient quasiconvexity is proved separately below.

candidates.label: Proposition 14.11

candidates.label: Theorem 4.1
candidates.name: MOTS barriers and the total trapped region
candidates.heading: Theorem 4.1 (MOTS barriers and the total trapped region).
candidates.statement: Let (N, g, Q) be a smooth compact three-dimensional initial data set with boundary Γ− ⊔ Γ+. Assume Γ+ is nonempty and has positive expansion with its normal out of N. The inner part Γ− may be empty; when it is present, assume its expansion is negative with its normal into N. Consider all smooth domains whose inner boundary is Γ− and whose remaining boundary Σ lies in the interior of N and satisfies ΘQ(Σ) ≤ 0. They avoid Γ+, and their normal on Σ points out of the domain. If their union is nonempty, its closure has a smooth compact embedded stable MOTS frontier in the interior, separating it from Γ+. This closure is itself the closure of such a domain and contains every domain in the defining class. If Γ− is nonempty, the two strict barriers also give a nonempty smooth embedded enclosing MOTS.

candidates.heading: Theorem 10.2 (Finite-component exterior equality rigidity).
candidates.statement: Let (M, g, K) be a smooth connected orientable complete initial data set without boundary, consisting of a compact core and finitely many asymptotically flat ends. On each end assume g − δ = O2(r−q), K = O1(r−1−q), with q > 1/2, and existing finite ADM flux limits. Assume that µ and |J|g are integrable and that µ ≥ |J|g everywhere. Choose an end and a finite nonempty disjoint union S = ℓ G i=1 Si, 1 ≤ ℓ < ∞, of compact connected smooth embedded two-sided surfaces without boundary, separating that end from a complementary region. Let Mext be the closure of the connected side toward the chosen end. Suppose that ∂Mext = S, that Mext has exactly this one end, and that, for the normal pointing into Mext: (i) every Si is a future MOTS, so HSi + trSi K = 0; (ii) S is outermost in the partial-coincidence sense of Definition 10.1; (iii) every enclosing cut in the closed exterior has area at least A = |S|g = Pℓ i=1 |Si|g > 0. Let (E, P) be the ADM vector of the chosen end. If (10.1) E > |P|δ, m = q E2 − |P|2 δ = s A 16π , then ℓ = 1 and S is diffeomorphic to a sphere. There is a proper smooth spacelike embedding of the entire original Mext into the maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime of mass m, inducing g and the given K for a consistent future unit normal. The chosen end approaches the corresponding spatial infinity. The image of S is a smooth cross-section of the corresponding future horizon or the bifurcation sphere. The embedding and its future normal are smooth up to S, and the image extends as a smooth spacelike hypersurface through that boundary.

There is a sequence of smooth data (gR, KR) on the same manifold, complete with the same compact boundary, satisfying the dominant energy condition and the same future boundary inequality, such that: (i) KR is compactly supported, and the ultimate end is an exact static Schwarzschild– Tangherlini spatial end; (ii) its energy is mR = m + o(1), its momentum is zero, and both constraint densities are integrable; (iii) A∗(gR) ≥ (1 − o(1))A∗(g). Every error here tends to zero as R → ∞ for the fixed original data and fixed timelike vector. No uniformity as E − |P| tends to zero is asserted or needed.

candidates.label: Proposition 24.8

candidates.heading: Proposition 24.8 (Closure of the end reduction).

candidates.label: Proposition 25.6
candidates.name: Geometric preparation
candidates.heading: Proposition 25.6 (Geometric preparation).
candidates.statement: For the prepared data satisfying (25.1), there are a closed connected exterior Ω ⊂ M with one end and nonempty compact smooth boundary B, two negative numbers cb, cw, and a decomposition of B into black and white components with the following properties. With the normal ν into Ω and PB = trB K, (25.13) H + PB = cb on black components, H − PB = cw on white components. The components come from closed total-region families Dc and Wc at right-continuity thresholds cb and cw, respectively. The white family is formed with the black region fixed, and is allowed to be empty. Every face has a disjoint smooth collar in Ω, with parameter s ≥ 0, | ds| > 0, and the corresponding expansion toward increasing s is at least cb or cw. There are a0 > 0, a compactly supported smooth function C, and a positive smooth weight ρ, equal to a positive constant times r−4−δ1 on the end, such that |C| ≤ a0 and, on smaller collars, (25.14) C = a0 − κBs on black collars, C = −a0 + κBs on white collars, κB > 0. Set (25.15) b− = cb − a0 < 0 < −cw + a0 = b+. Every real-valued function h taking values in [b−, b+] on supp K∩Ω satisfies the following inequality on Ω: (25.16) |(h + C)τ| + | dC|g + ρ ≤ µ − |J|g, τ = trg K. There is a smooth compactly supported extension b on Ω of the boundary values b− on black faces and b+ on white faces, constant on smaller collars. Finally, every smooth enclosing cut of B in Ω has g-volume at least A∗.

candidates.statement: On the real linear space of all smooth TT seeds with the prescribed decay, the first deficit coefficient is zero and the second coefficient c2[q] is a continuous, rotation-invariant, nonnegative quadratic form. manuscripts.title: The Kerr–Newman Penrose Inequality for Axisymmetric Electrovacuum Exteriors

candidates.label: Theorem 2.2
candidates.name: Penrose inequality and nondegenerate rigidity
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.2 (Penrose inequality and nondegenerate rigidity).
candidates.statement: Under the hypotheses of this section, m2 ≥ A 16π + Q2 2 + π(Q4 + 4J2) A . (2.17) If A > 4π p Q4 + 4J2 and equality holds, the original exterior (Ω, g, K, Ef, Bf) admits a smooth spacelike embedding into the domain of outer communication together with the appropriate future horizon of a subextremal dyonic Kerr–Newman spacetime with mass m, angular momentum J, and charges Qe, Qb, in the conventions above. The induced metric, second fundamental form with a consistent future normal, and induced fields agree with the given data. The end approaches the corresponding spatial infinity. The embedding and normal extend smoothly to S, which maps to a smooth future-horizon cross-section or to the bifurcation sphere. Conversely, every such Kerr–Newman exterior slice satisfying all the hypotheses and meeting that horizon attains equality. Nonconstant time graphs and nonzero second fundamental forms are permitted.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.4

candidates.heading: Proposition 3.4 (Polarization).
candidates.statement: The data (g0, k0) extend smoothly through the axis, have the stated asymptotic decay, and have the same ADM energy as (g, K). For every invariant surface, its area and future expansion are unchanged. Let µ0, J0 be the constraint densities of (g0, k0), with J0 a covector. Write dA = fadAh and set s = (−Be, Ee, −Xfa/2). Then 16πµ0 = 2 |DX|2 g0 + |s|2 , 8πJ0 = 2s · DX. (3.9) The source combinations on the right are smooth across the axis. On a signed axis tube s1, s2 are odd of order y, and s3 is even of order y2. In particular the polarized data satisfy the dominant energy condition.

candidates.heading: Proposition 3.5 (Einstein–wave-map quotient).
candidates.statement: For an invariant electrovacuum spacetime the axial potentials satisfy dχ = −ιηF, dψ = ιη ∗4 F, ω = −1 2X3 ∗H dA, DX(n) = s, (3.11) on every invariant spacelike slice, where n is its horizontal future unit normal. With Φ = (u, ψ, χ, z), the equations reduce to Ricγ = 2Φ∗ G, □γΦ = 0. (3.12) The second expression is the wave-map tension for the target G. Conversely, these reduced equations reconstruct locally an invariant Einstein–Maxwell metric and field, up to angular and electromagnetic gauge. Their slice data recover the original metric, tensor, and fields from the polarized data, the potentials, and their normal velocities.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.8

candidates.heading: Proposition 3.8 (Model map and boundary data).
candidates.statement: Let Φ∗ be the map of Proposition 3.5 for Equation (3.19), with axis values Equation (3.5). Its ADM energy is M, its angular momentum in the present convention is J = −aM, its charges are Q, 0, and its horizon area is 4πR2. It is independent of Killing time. Define w = sinh σ sin ϑ, q∗ = 1 2 log(W sin2 ϑ). With Euclidean strip derivatives, it satisfies divG(w dΦ∗) = 0, −∆q∗ = |∂Φ∗|2 G, q∗(0, ϑ) = log(R2 sin ϑ). (3.20) The canonical slice and its tensor and fields extend smoothly to the bifurcation sphere, including the ordinary axis poles. Its potentials have the regularity of Lemma 3.3; their renormalized components and u∗ − log sin ϑ have bounded derivatives on compact closed strip ranges.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.1
candidates.name: Riemannian comparison
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.1 (Riemannian comparison).
candidates.statement: Let Ωr be the closure of the component toward infinity obtained by removing finitely many smooth compact invariant obstacles from a rotation exterior as in the axial reduction. The omitted region includes the original inner side, and ∂Ωr is nonempty. Suppose the following hold. candidates.heading: Theorem 2.4 (AF Riemannian Penrose inequality).

Assume Rh ≥ 0, h − δ = O2(|y|−β) for some β > 1/2, and Rh = O(|y|−q) for some q > 3. If the total boundary area is A, then mAF(h) ≥ √︂ A/(16π). (2.2) Disconnected boundary is allowed.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.5
candidates.name: Scalar local estimates
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.5 (Scalar local estimates).
candidates.statement: On fixed coordinate balls in dimension three the following estimates hold, with constants depending on the indicated ellipticity, coefficient, and geometry bounds. (i) Bounded measurable uniformly elliptic divergence matrices admit local subsolution bounds, weak Harnack estimates for nonnegative supersolutions, and inhomogeneous Harnack and Hölder estimates for nonnegative solutions. Bounded divergence drifts multiplying the un- known, vector forcing in Lq, q > 3, and scalar forcing in Lp, p > 3/2, are permitted in the corresponding estimates. (ii) For Laplace equations with uniformly positive Lipschitz metric coefficients in interior or flattened smooth boundary charts, divergence forcing in Lq gives local W1,q estimates. Scalar forcing in L2 can be included for 3 < q < 6. The same statements hold with local zero Dirichlet data or natural Neumann data, with the divergence forcing included in the conormal current. A boundary datum in Lp1 , p1 > 2, permits a choice 3 < q < 3p1/2 sufficiently close to 3. (iii) Smooth-coefficient scalar Dirichlet and conormal problems have the usual Schauder estimates, including divergence-form C1,γ estimates when the uniformly elliptic coefficients and vector forcing are Cγ, with boundary data of the corresponding regularity. These estimates are used only after their coefficient hypotheses have been obtained. (iv) For a bounded measurable symmetric uniformly elliptic matrix a on a ball, its positive Dirichlet Green kernel is bounded above by C|z − z′|−1, and below by c|z − z′|−1 when the pole and the nearby evaluation point lie in a fixed smaller ball.

The cap-only enclosure E0 is a smooth precompact strictly outward-minimizing set, with minimal boundary disjoint from O, every component meeting O, and Scalˆ︁ h ≥ −CR outside E0. (4.19) In the piecewise case this is required for surfaces having zero area in the joining surface. For every 0 < ε < 1 there are positive tolerances η0, q0, δ0 and v0, depending only on ε, A∗, CR and the integer b2 in (4.1), with the following consequence. If η ≤ η0, q ≤ q0, 0 < δ ≤ δ0, and ∫︂ {x<1−δ} ρ3/2 W dVgbase < v0, (4.20) then |∂E0|ˆ︁ h ≥ (1 − ε)A∗. (4.21) The tolerances are uniform over all comparisons satisfying these conditions; the geometry and initial area of E0 may vary.

There are exact smooth complete vacuum data dT ∈ D on the whole bridge with pm(dT −d) → 0. They agree with d on the other end, the connecting region, and an expanding protected ball on the selected end. The permitted exterior correction tail is retained. 2. An exact exterior evolution of dT reaches the required part of S, with overlapping collars and strict outflow margins. In the fixed background wave-map description its entry spacetime jets differ from g + hp by O(A2 T eηoutT ). Here hp = AT tr. rev.g Re  eiλv J∗ X j=0 λ−j pj   . (4.3) The leading coefficient is real, trace-free, and annihilates L0. On the entire observation box QT , |(p0)AB|γ ≥ e−o(T) . (4.4) At every fixed required base order the ordinary mixed coordinate jets of the normalized amplitude components are eo(T), and the linearized Ricci and gauge errors have arbitrarily high inverse- frequency accuracy. 3. There is a metric ḡ exactly of double-null form, with fields γ̄, log Ā, b̄ and their exact geo- metric derived fields. Through order N, its differences from the background fields, including q−1∂vb, are O(AT eηoutT ). Its defects in the null structure and angular equations (5.4)–(5.7) are O(A2 T eηoutT ). If the actual exterior induced data are written in double-null coordinates initialized by the background values on S, their full entry jets differ from this template by the same quadratic bound. All entry discrepancies and all template changes and defects vanish for v < (1 −ν)T. Any additional finite initial or residual jet buffers may be included in N. Positive frequency powers at these base orders are independent of the later orders used to improve linear accuracy. At the finitely many high entry orders ultimately requested by Theorem 5.1, the actual fields have eo(T) bounds.

candidates.label: Theorem 5.1
candidates.name: Finite double-null experiment
candidates.heading: Theorem 5.1 (Finite double-null experiment).
candidates.statement: For every fixed background and branch tube in Lemma 2.4, every finite m, s, and every sufficiently small fixed c > 0, the parameters in Propo- sition 4.1 can be chosen so that its exact entry data have a smooth vacuum development on Equation (5.1) in the double-null gauge initialized there. The relative lapse and the sphere metric remain positive and uniformly nondegenerate. For U = (γ, log A, b, χ0, χ1, ℓ0, ℓ1, ξ0, ξ1) one has, in a fixed sphere atlas and ordinary coordinate derivatives, max |I|≤s ∥∂I (U′ − Ū)∥L∞(ΩT ) ≤ e−(1+c)αT (5.2) for all sufficiently large T in the selected experiment sequence. The same conclusion holds for q−1∂vb′ − q−1∂vb̄ at any preassigned finite order, after increasing the finite order budget. The individual ordinary jets of the primed relative fields through every order used in the experiment are eo(T), uniformly for this moving family. The exact solution and the template equal the background where v < (1 − ν)T. The exact solution agrees on an entry collar, by local geometric uniqueness, with the actual exterior solution of Proposition 4.1.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.3

candidates.heading: Proposition 3.8 (Comparison development and first runout).
candidates.statement: After decreasing the defining p10 radius of U, each d ∈ U has a smooth globally hyperbolic vacuum comparison development Pd containing the whole bridge Σ as a Cauchy hypersurface and embedded openly and isometrically in Md. It contains a spacelike cylinder S and its full future product wedge, with coordinates t = (u + v)/2 ≥ 0, x = (v − u)/2 ∈ R, θ ∈ S2, in which g = −2a du dv + γAB(dθA − bA du)(dθB − bB du), a = qA, q = q0e−κ(u+v) , q0, κ > 0. (3.9) The coefficients A±1 and γ±1 are uniformly bounded, with γ uniformly comparable to a fixed round sphere metric. Every seed with Td(w) < ∞ crosses S before its first runout from Pd, and that first runout has exactly one of the following coordinate limits: first branch: u → u∗ < ∞, v → +∞, second branch: v → v∗ < ∞, u → +∞, corner: u → +∞, v → +∞. (3.10) These alternatives describe limiting coordinate regimes; they do not adjoin boundary points or identify Pd with Md.

candidates.heading: Proposition 3.10 (Corner seeds have measure zero).

candidates.heading: Corollary 3.11 (A branch seed for every passing test).

After exchanging the optical labels and preparing the angular coordinates as in [20, Lemma 7.8], the branch can be written u → u∗ < ∞, v → ∞. The seed is still the same initial seed in O.

candidates.name: All-spin geometric interface
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.2 (All-spin geometric interface).
candidates.statement: There is a choice of ϵ > 0, depending only on the fixed Kerr center and the fixed preparation, such that every p10(d − d∗) < ϵ in the stated smooth symbol class has the following properties. 1. The cylinder S in Proposition 3.8 has a smooth vacuum development on the full product wedge [0, ∞)t ×Rx ×S2 in Equation (4.1). The quantities A±1, γ±1 are uniformly bounded in angular H6, and ξi, a−1∂vb in angular H5. There are nonnegative functions gi(yi) with summable unit-cell suprema such that, in the indicated low angular norms, ∥χi, ℓi + κ∥H4 ≤ C(q + gi(yi)), ∥b∥H5 ≤ C(q + g0(u)). (4.3) 2. The following quantities are uniformly bounded, and tend to zero when t, |u|, |v| → ∞: ∥b∥H5 + X i ∥χi, ℓi + κ∥H4 , 1 X k=0 ∥∂yk b∥H2 + X i ∥∂yk χi, ∂yk ℓi∥H2 ! , 1 X k=0 (∥∂yk γ∥H4 + ∥∂yk log a + κ∥H4 ) . (4.4) In particular D log a, Dγ, b, Db are uniformly bounded. 17 3. For each fixed U ∈ R, C > 0, and finite order, all ordinary derivatives of γ±1 , log A, b, a−1 ∂vb (4.5) are bounded by eo(T) on t ≥ 0, yd ≤ U, yl ≤ CT, {d, l} = {0, 1}. (4.6) This includes every restriction and coordinate-path subsegment. Every fixed derivative of a, √ a, or ∂vb retains, respectively, the factor a, √ a, or a. 4. Either branch can be put in the convention v → ∞, u → u∗ < ∞. Exchanging the optical labels and preparing the angular coordinates anew preserves all these conclusions on the same product spacetime and initial cylinder. Only p10 is required small; no higher seminorm, radiation coefficient, or curvature measured by a timelike observer is required small or bounded.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.4
candidates.name: Entry timing, escape, and flow estimates
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.4 (Entry timing, escape, and flow estimates).
candidates.statement: On either prepared end use regular exterior time te, co-moving coordinates y, and lab coordinates z = y + Ce(te), with fixed sup |C′ e| ≤ s∗ < 1/10, after decreasing ϵ if needed. The relevant slice te = 0 agrees with the original bridge sufficiently far out. There is a preparation parameter I with 0 < cI ≤ I′ ≤ CI and I(tT ) = T. The launch patch near v = x = T on S occurs at te = tT + O(1), and tT ≍ T. A fixed enlargement is contained in te ≤ tT + C2. Its selected-end portion v < (1 − ν0)T is earlier by at least cν0T − O(1) for each fixed ν0 > 0. The exterior metric has uniformly regular spacelike temporal levels. Its first and second ordinary lab derivatives are bounded on the computing region and become arbitrarily small at sufficiently large co-radius, uniformly in time. Every fixed mixed jet on the used time and radius ranges O(1 + T) is eo(T). Entry charts have a noncharacteristic collar with controlled low jets and subexponential fixed higher jets; the inner exit has a strict margin deeper than the entry cylinder. The null covectors dv launched on a sufficiently small fixed patch at this entry escape towards the past to the same original end. For each fixed β > 0, after fixing a sufficiently large radius and taking T large, their bridge arrival points satisfy (1 − β)tT < |z − z∗| < (1 + β)tT , z∗ = Ce(tT ). (4.11) The entry crossing is unique and transverse, and separated from other used ray portions outside a uniform collar. Every fixed Hamiltonian flow jet, including launch-center derivatives and the propagators on all subsegments, is eo(T). Tensor parallel transport and its inverse are bounded. These assertions hold on short past and future launch enlargements through the deeper exit.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.6
candidates.name: Linear packet and exterior beam
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.6 (Linear packet and exterior beam).
candidates.statement: Fix any finite list of output derivative orders, including an exterior base buffer Nb. For every fixed ζ > 0 and every subsequently prescribed inverse accuracy M1, sufficiently high finite transport and Taylor orders yield a real interior tensor hp T and a real exterior tensor hB T with the following properties. candidates.label: Corollary 4.8
candidates.name: Linear construction at any exponentially small amplitude

candidates.statement: Fix any α > 0 and put AT = e−αT . With this substitution, all linear conclusions of Proposition 4.6 hold, with the same order of finite output, frequency and inverse-accuracy choices. The branch observer needs no bounded-curvature hypothesis.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.1
candidates.name: Signed preparation and entry
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.1 (Signed preparation and entry).
candidates.statement: Fix a finite data order m ≥ 10, a finite entry order r, a loss η > 0, and 0 < ν0 < 1. After fixing all the finite derivative orders needed below, one can choose ζ > 0 and then the finite formal accuracy orders in Proposition 4.6 so that the following hold for all sufficiently large parameters T in the packet sequence. There are smooth positive complete vacuum data d± T ∈ D on the whole bridge, with pm(d± T − d) −→ 0. (5.2) 27 In particular d± T ∈ U for large T. They agree exactly with d on the other end, the connecting region, and a protected region containing every fixed compact subset for large T. On the selected asymptotic end the protected ball is BT = {|z − z∗| < ρT }, z∗ = Ce(tT ), ρT = (1 − 2β)tT , (5.3) where β > 0 is fixed sufficiently small. The data have the weight-one metric and weight-two second- form symbol bounds at every order. Their full correction tails are retained; asymptotic coefficients are allowed to change. Ordinary exterior vacuum evolutions g± T , in exact wave-map gauge with the same target g, exist on the finite domains needed to reach ST , with fixed overlap margins and strict future-outflow artificial boundaries. Set H± T = \ g± T − g, F± T = H± T ∓ qT on the entry collar. Then Jr,T (F± T ) ≤ A2 T eηT , Jr,T (F+ T − F− T ) ≤ A3 T eηT . (5.4) The exact changes, packet, and errors vanish on the earlier needed entry interval v < (1 − ν0)T. In particular, r = 61 is permitted, with an arbitrarily small prescribed loss. The scaled linear deep residual can simultaneously be at most e−4κT through order 60, or at any other finite orders fixed in advance. The same statement holds for the separately prepared exchanged branch.

candidates.statement: Fix any α > 0. Replace the amplitude in this section by AT = e−αT and use Corollary 4.8. For every fixed data order m, entry order r, loss η > 0 and late-support fraction 0 < ν0 < 1, the conclusions of Proposition 5.1 hold after choosing the frequency exponent sufficiently small and the inverse accuracy sufficiently large. This assertion ends at the entry cylinder.

candidates.heading: Proposition 6.1 (Signed interior experiment).
candidates.statement: Fix 0 < δ < κ/32 and the prescribed finite data seminorm. Use Proposition 4.6 and Proposition 5.1 with sufficiently high fixed orders, sufficiently small losses and late support parameter, and sufficiently accurate linear residuals. For sufficiently small fixed ζ > 0 and sufficiently large T, the two entry data have smooth vacuum evolutions g± T on the strict domain (6.1), in wave-map gauge with target g. Let H± T be the relative arrays of g± T − g, and put F± T = H± T ∓ qT , Fodd T = F+ T − F− T . Then ∥F± T ∥C30 mix(ΩT ) ≤ e(κ−2α+δ)T , ∥Fodd T ∥C2 mix(ΩT ) ≤ e(κ−3α+δ)T + e(2κ−4α+δ)T . (6.2) The exact changes and all three error fields have support in v ≥ (1 − ν0)T − o(1). The time slices remain spacelike and the two moving side faces remain strict future exits. Moreover, for some c > 0, ∥H± T ∥C30 mix ≤ e−(κ/2+c)T , eo(T) ∥Fodd T ∥C2 mix + X ± ∥H± T ∥2 C2 mix ! = o(AT ). (6.3) Here every subexponential factor is at a fixed finite order. No higher seminorm of the fixed smooth background is required to be small.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.1
candidates.name: Whole-bridge attachment
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.1 (Whole-bridge attachment).
candidates.statement: For all sufficiently large finite T, there is a smooth time-oriented vacuum development N± T of the entire datum d± T with Σ as a Cauchy hypersurface. It contains the constructed finite observation, restricted within its construction margins, and an optical-coordinate box about pT , of fixed sufficiently small coordinate radii independent of T, in I+ N± T (Σ). It admits a time-orientation-preserving open isometric embedding into Md± T that preserves the initial-data embedding. The full physical constraint-correction tail is part of its initial data.

candidates.statement: At pT put U± T = I± T U. There are seeds w± T → w on Σ whose future unit geodesics in Md± T reach pT with tangent U± T , at finite positive proper times strictly before their full-MGHD future durations. In particular w± T belong to the original open seed set for all sufficiently large T. Choose an angular orthonormal frame eA near pT , including the packet polarization direction at the center, and set E± 0 = I± T L0, E± 1 = a−1 I± T L1, E± A = I± T eA. (7.20) At pT the Euclidean norm of components in this frame and the parallel positive test norm kd± T ,w± T are uniformly equivalent, with constants independent of T. Their induced operator norms are uniformly equivalent as well.
