manuscripts.title: Quantitative Near-Kerr Evolution and Generic C2 Future Inextendibility

candidates.label: Theorem 1.2
candidates.name: Local C2 strong cosmic censorship
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.2 (Local C2 strong cosmic censorship).
candidates.statement: For every fixed M > 0 and 0 < a < M, there exists ϵ > 0 such that the data in Uϵ = {d ∈ D : p10(d − (h∗, K∗)) < ϵ} whose full maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum developments admit a C2 future extension form a meagre subset of Uϵ. Equivalently, the future-inextendible data contain a countable intersection of relatively open dense subsets of Uϵ.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.5
candidates.name: Regular-exit covering
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.5 (Regular-exit covering).
candidates.statement: If d ∈ Uϵ admits a C2 future extension, there exist O ∈ O and N ≥ 1 such that d ∈ A(O, N) and every seed in O reaches its finite MGHD endpoint on a regular ambient geodesic arc. Here regular means that position and unit tangent continue to and through the endpoint.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.6
candidates.name: Finite-observation criterion
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.6 (Finite-observation criterion).
candidates.statement: Suppose a single ϵ > 0 has the following property. For every O ∈ O, N ≥ 1, d ∈ B(O, N), integer m ≥ 10 and η > 0, there exist d′ ∈ Uϵ, w′ ∈ O, and 0 ≤ τ < Td′ (w′) such that pm(d′ − d) < η, Qd′ (w′ , τ) > N. Then Theorem 1.2 holds for this ϵ.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.6
candidates.name: Normally hyperbolic trapping with escape
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.6 (Normally hyperbolic trapping with escape).
candidates.statement: For each fixed subextremal Kerr metric, the energy-normalized photon trap is symplectically transverse of codimension two and has smooth local stable and unstable surfaces. Their normal expansion and contraction rates are bounded away from zero. All fixed-order tangent derivatives grow subexponentially, so the normal rates dominate the tangent dynamics at every fixed order. These properties hold on a sufficiently small interval of nearby levels of the separated fixed-frequency symbol. A departing radial tail escapes the radial trapping neighborhood and cannot return along a homoclinic orbit.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.7
candidates.name: An elliptic cone containing the projected trap
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.7 (An elliptic cone containing the projected trap).
candidates.statement: Choose G′ = 1 throughout the photon region. The union of the spatial projections of both trapped null sheets is contained, with a positive margin, in a spatial conic neighborhood T with compact base support separated from the horizon and from both spatial ends of the estimates. On this neighborhood, bij (y)ηiηj ≥ c|η|2 (3.28) for some c > 0 and any fixed auxiliary cotangent norm on the compact base support. Both temporal roots there are nonzero and have absolute values comparable to |η|. One can choose nested smaller and larger conic neighborhoods with these properties, and the same choices work after sufficiently small changes of exact Kerr parameters and stationary charts.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.1
candidates.name: Local spectral input
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.1 (Local spectral input).
candidates.statement: On the fixed subextremal Kerr cylinder there are arbitrarily small, stationary, smooth, compactly based bundle-map modifications of harmonic gauge and of its symmetric-gradient partner with these properties. 1. The stationary gauge-potential operator, obtained by applying the modified gauge to a pure Lie derivative, is invertible at decay strictly between the powers 1 and r−1. 2. The modified linearized reduced vacuum operator has outgoing inversion at nonzero frequency in the closed physical half-plane. Its bounded-frequency estimates, with a weaker compact error, are uniform down to zero in the weight interval −3/2 < ℓ < −1/2. Its zero-frequency realization has index zero and a seven-dimensional kernel: four gauge-corrected Kerr variations and three translations. 3. In outgoing time, a polynomial mode with coefficients of order O(r−1+) has translation leading coefficient if its degree is one. There are no such modes of degree at least two. For tensors one may take s > 5/2, with strict margin, also sufficient for gauge potentials. The uniform near-zero equation norm is Hs−1,ℓ+2 b . At nonzero frequency the outgoing conditions are ℓ < −1/2 and s + ℓ > −1/2.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.3
candidates.name: Stationary estimates
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.3 (Stationary estimates).
candidates.statement: For sufficiently large Λ, the conically modified base operator has the following estimates. 1. Bounded-frequency estimates with weaker compact errors persist uniformly as Λ → ∞, at the orders and zero-frequency weights of Proposition 4.1. The stationary index is zero, and kernel and cokernel are upper semicontinuous. On closed bounded bands excluding zero, the physical estimates persist without compact error, up to Re ζ ↓ 0. 2. For every fixed strip 0 ≤ Re ζ ≤ D∗ and fixed admissible order, there are polynomial high- frequency bounds without kernel, with threshold independent of sufficiently large Λ. These include the compact Hs estimate from Hs−1, for s = 5 or a fixed higher admissible order, the supported dual solution estimate of order 1 − s, and ⟨r⟩−1/2−ι (v, ∂yv) ∈ L2 for the physical transpose with a compact smooth source, with polynomial frequency cost. 3. Zero-frequency estimates, including those for gauge potentials, persist uniformly for nearby exact Kerr principal metrics in smooth stationary, asymptotically affine charts of the prescribed 24 type. Fixed smooth finite-dimensional supplements remove their kernel and cokernel locally in parameters. The same-sign outgoing transpose has the a priori estimate and index stated in Lemma 4.4.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.6
candidates.name: Exact stationary families and supplements
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.6 (Exact stationary families and supplements).
candidates.statement: For small p = (m, v) ∈ R4 × R3 there is a smooth family Gp of exact diffeomorphic stationary Kerr metrics with G0 = b, tangent directions H, LW b, and symbol asymptote Gp − ηv = O(r−1 ), ηv = −(1 − |v|2 )dt2 − 2vi dyi dt + |dy|2 . (4.12) Let Lp(0) denote the stationary linear reduced operator at metric and target Gp. It has seven independent decaying modes and ten further independent stationary homogeneous metric modes with constant tensor asymptotes. There are no additional dimensions at any growth power strictly between 0 and 1. There exist a fixed compact smooth seven-vector functional ℓ, smooth ten-vector functionals ℓp C, and a smooth list HC(p) of the ten additional modes, satisfying ℓ(H, J) = I, ℓHC(p) = 0, ℓp CHC(p) = I, with ℓp C annihilating the seven decaying modes. Their supports can be fixed outside a physical trapping neighborhood. There is a second smooth exact stationary Kerr family Gp,c, c ∈ R10 small, with Gp,0 = Gp, ∂cGp,0 = HC(p). (4.13) 30 The gauge calibration extends smoothly to both families. The frozen gauge of Gp,c relative to Gp is O(c2) on fixed compact sets.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.11
candidates.name: Local evolution and vacuum initialization
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.11 (Local evolution and vacuum initialization).
candidates.statement: The reduced equation (4.2), (4.22), with retarded feedback (4.21), has smooth local evolution for smooth initial wave data small in E10. It continues on finite time intervals while E10 remains bounded, the parameters stay in their chosen small range, the normalized acceleration and implicit-coordinate inverses stay uniformly controlled, and the spacelike and strict outflow margins remain positive. Smooth higher orders propagate on bounded time intervals; these higher seminorms need only be finite. For smooth vacuum constraint data, the initial lapse and shift derivatives can be chosen so that Υ and its first normal derivative vanish initially. The resulting evolution is vacuum.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.13
candidates.name: Retarded stationary tests
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.13 (Retarded stationary tests).
candidates.statement: Fix a compact test support and a finite number of required angular derivatives. There are a sufficiently high fixed test Sobolev order q∗ and a finite polynomial degree N∗ with the following property. Choose the filter order P sufficiently large and σ0 > 0 sufficiently small, then take Λ, R sufficiently large in the order specified below. For 0 < Re ζ ≤ D∗ on that strip and a compactly supported test f of order q∗, the spatial transpose equation MR(ζ)t v∗ = f has a solution satisfying ∥v∗∥Ḣ−4(K) ≤ CR3ι ⟨ζ⟩N∗ ∥f∥Hq∗ , (4.33) ∥(v∗, ry(∂ry + ζ)v∗)∥L2 ω ≤ Cr−1+ι y R3ι ⟨ζ⟩N∗ ∥f∥Hq∗ (ry ≫ 1). (4.34) Here K is any prescribed fixed compact reach, and the second bound includes the prescribed angular derivatives. The bounds are uniform down to Re ζ ↓ 0 on a fixed strip reaching a forward Laplace line. The slack ι > 0 can be arbitrarily small without making N∗ diverge. The associated tested operators are retarded.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.1
candidates.name: Low-frequency transfer
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.1 (Low-frequency transfer).
candidates.statement: Under the simultaneous finite-slab budgets above, there is κ0 > 0 such that, after choosing R and then T0 sufficiently large, l ≤ CR−κ0 (KR + F) + Cfix(ein + N2 ). (5.7) The exponent can be fixed before enlarging any prior compact reach. Such enlargements change constants but not the available radius gain.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.2
candidates.name: Frozen energy
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.2 (Frozen energy).
candidates.statement: Fix a smooth nearby stationary parameter pair (p, c) and an integer s ≥ 8. The frozen operator Lp,c admits a positive time-local first-jet energy, uniformly for nearby parameters, with full endpoint orders Hs ⊕ Hs−1. On each fixed interior reach its favorable derivative controls ∥Y∥2 Hs−3/2 + ∥BntY∥2 Hs−1 − Cs∥Y∥2 Hs−2(enlarged), Y = (⟨Dy⟩U, DtU), Dt = −i∂t. (5.10) It also controls full mixed physical-nontrapping orders after equation recovery. At the inner and outer differential regions the energy is an ordinary wave current with strict bulk sign and an exiting inner flux. All remaining compact derivative errors have total field order at most s − 1. The compact additions to the differential currents have strictly interior spatial kernel support.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.3
candidates.name: Sliced estimates
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.3 (Sliced estimates).
candidates.statement: On any fixed enlarged compact reach, the simultaneous budgets imply Sa ≤ C(R0)KR + CF + Cfix(ein + N2 ), C independent of R0, (5.16) ∥gco − Gp,c∥L2 AS H8 loc ≤ Cloc(KR + F + Sa) + Cfix(ein + N2 ). (5.17) The second estimate includes mixed jets of total order eight, and one extra time derivative with the same mixed order on fixed sets outside the physical trapping neighborhood. This extra derivative will supply the mixed time-radial trace in (7.11) when the exterior solution is restricted to the interior entry cylinder. Constants on these fixed reaches are independent of the upper radius R.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.4
candidates.name: Actual-principal comparison
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.4 (Actual-principal comparison).
candidates.statement: For each level (U, s, Ai) in (5.1), let dαβ M be the change from ḡ to g of the differential order-two wave coefficient in stationary normalization. On fixed compact reaches the reduced equation has the form Lp(t),c(t)U + dαβ M ∂αβU = Slin i + Serr i , Slin i = ±Q(∂t)bi, bi = a, a, a′ , (5.22) 51 up to common normalizations, where Serr i ∈ L1 Ai Hs−1 + L2 Ai Hs−1/2 , ∥Serr i ∥ ≤ CfixN2 + Cfixein. (5.23) On larger bounded differential annuli only L2 Ai Hs−1 is required. There is an actual-principal correction of the frozen energy whose additional integrated derivative errors are bounded in squared estimates by CfixN3, up to input terms. The frozen half-loss bulk and directional improvement remain on the left side of that estimate.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.5
candidates.name: Compact high estimate
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.5 (Compact high estimate).
candidates.statement: Under the simultaneous finite-slab budgets, for some κ > 0, KR ≤ CR−κ (F + KR) + Cfix ( ein + N3/2 + (einN)1/2) . (5.31) The acceleration and sliced static bounds enter this estimate only as coefficient smallness and nonlinear errors, not as additional linear forcing terms. The choices are the stationary energy parameters, then a sufficiently large R, then the plateau T0, and finally the bootstrap and data smallness.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.6
candidates.name: Subexponential smooth bounds
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.6 (Subexponential smooth bounds).
candidates.statement: Assume the global base bounds resulting from the compact-far closure. For every fixed C0 > 0, every fixed smooth order, and every σ > 0, all metric, coefficient and parameter norms at that order on 0 ≤ t ≤ T′ , ry ≤ C0(1 + T′ ) are bounded by CσeσT′ . The constant may depend on the smooth datum, the order and C0, but the base neighborhood and fixed filter do not. We denote these bounds by eo(T′).

candidates.label: Proposition 6.3
candidates.name: Far estimate
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.3 (Far estimate).
candidates.statement: After giving the finitely many commuted energies fixed hierarchy weights, there is c1 > 0 such that F ≤ oR0 (1)(F + Sa) + C(R0)KR + Cfix ( input errors + N1+c1 ) . (6.25) The coefficient denoted by oR0 (1) tends to zero as R0 → ∞, independently of the upper compact matching radius R. The input errors vanish with ein, uniformly on bounded small bootstrap ranges.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.4
candidates.name: Simultaneous closure
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.4 (Simultaneous closure).
candidates.statement: For each fixed strictly subextremal center and fixed computing cylinders, there is a base smallness threshold depending only on the finite p10 input such that the compact, far, static, and modulation bounds hold on every finite slab. They yield global smooth vacuum evolution on both computing cylinders. Every fixed higher-order bound of Proposition 5.6 then holds with datum- and order-dependent constants; those higher seminorms need only be finite.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.3
candidates.name: Cylinder data and their derivative budget
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.3 (Cylinder data and their derivative budget).
candidates.statement: Start actual eikonal coordinates on the prepared cylinder with y0 = −x, y1 = x, and transport its prepared angular labels along L1. For sufficiently small data in the common base neighborhood, the sum of unit-x-cell supremum norms of the differences from frozen profiles is at most an arbitrarily prescribed small number eS for A, log A, γ, b, χi, ℓi, ξi in angular H6, γ in angular H7, ∂x(χi, ℓi, ξi, b)|S in angular H2. (7.10) Here ∂x is tangent to the cylinder at fixed prepared angle, and the comparison in the last line uses frozen differentiation. The sum of cell suprema of σ0 is also at most CeS. At each fixed higher order, these initial quantities and their parameter jets on |x| ≤ CT are bounded by eo(T) for every fixed C > 0. The low smallness depends only on the common base-order neighborhood; constants may depend on the already fixed q0 and coordinate choices. Higher-order constants may depend on the individual smooth datum.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.4
candidates.name: Uniform low characteristic estimates
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.4 (Uniform low characteristic estimates).
candidates.statement: Choose q0 sufficiently small in terms of the uniform profile constants, and then choose eS sufficiently small. On every smooth finite past diamond satisfying the entry assumptions, E + R + X + Db + P + S ≤ C(q0)eS. (7.20) The metrics A, γ and their inverses remain uniformly bounded and nondegenerate at the indicated low orders. The constants are independent of the location and size of the diamond.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.5
candidates.name: Pure jets and flank limits
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.5 (Pure jets and flank limits).
candidates.statement: Under the assumptions of Proposition 7.4, the sum of unit-yi-cell suprema of sup yj ( |Liχi − ̂ Liχi|2 + |Liℓi − ̂ Liℓi|2 ) (7.32) is at most CeS. For i = 0 the same holds for ∂y0 b − ∂fr y0 ̂ b in angular H2. On a full wedge obtained by exhaustion, A±1, γ±1 are uniformly bounded in H6 and ξi, a−1∂y1 b in H5, and |b|5 + ∑ i |(χi, ℓi + κ)|4 −→ 0, 1 ∑ k=0 ( |∂yk b|2 + ∑ i |∂yk (χi, ℓi)|2 + |∂yk γ|4 + |∂yk log a + κ|4 ) −→ 0 (7.33) as s → ∞ and |y0|, |y1| → ∞. All displayed quantities are uniformly bounded elsewhere. No smallness of the limiting angular metric or rescaled torsion is asserted.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.6
candidates.name: Higher estimates
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.6 (Higher estimates).
candidates.statement: Assume the entry bounds of Proposition 7.3 and the low estimates on smooth finite past diamonds. 1. On every fixed finite diamond, all fixed ordinary coordinate derivatives of γ±1, log A, b, a−1∂y1 b have finite bounds depending only on the corresponding smooth initial norms, the low bounds, and that diamond. 2. If the solution and its uniformly summed low estimates are defined on the full wedge, fix U ∈ R, C > 0, and either labeling {d, l} = {0, 1}. On s ≥ 0, yd ≤ U, yl ≤ CT, (7.37) every fixed ordinary coordinate derivative of γ±1, log A, b, a−1∂y1 b is bounded by eo(T). The same bounds hold on all restrictions and coordinate-path subsegments of this domain. Neither conclusion requires any higher-order initial norm to be small.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.7
candidates.name: Continuation from the full cylinder
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.7 (Continuation from the full cylinder).
candidates.statement: The smooth vacuum cylinder data of Proposition 7.3 have a smooth development on the full product wedge {s ≥ 0} × Rx × S2 in the gauge (7.1). It satisfies Propositions 7.4, 7.5, and both conclusions of Proposition 7.6. With a sufficiently small past collar, S is a Cauchy surface for this development. The construction does not identify this region with the whole maximal globally hyperbolic development.

candidates.label: Proposition 8.2
candidates.name: The comparison development
candidates.heading: Proposition 8.2 (The comparison development).
candidates.statement: There is a single sufficiently small p10 neighbor- hood such that, for each datum d in it, the preceding exterior and interior solutions assemble with the finite bridge evolution into a smooth time-oriented vacuum development Pd with the complete bridge Σ as a Cauchy surface. It contains an entire spacelike cylinder S ≃ R × S2 carrying the entry data of Section 7, followed by its full product double-null wedge. There is a time-orientation-preserving open isometric embedding Pd ˓→ Md into the full MGHD of d.

candidates.label: Proposition 8.5
candidates.name: No finite exterior runout
candidates.heading: Proposition 8.5 (No finite exterior runout).
candidates.statement: A future unit timelike geodesic from Σ, inextendible as a geodesic in Pd, which never crosses S has infinite future proper duration.

candidates.label: Corollary 8.6
candidates.name: First-runout classification
candidates.heading: Corollary 8.6 (First-runout classification).
candidates.statement: Let a future unit timelike geodesic from Σ have finite maximal future proper duration in Md. Follow its initial connected portion in Pd up to first runout. It crosses S, and its first runout has exactly one of the behaviors (8.20).

candidates.label: Proposition 8.8
candidates.name: A branch seed in the original open family
candidates.heading: Proposition 8.8 (A branch seed in the original open family).
candidates.statement: Let d belong to the fixed base neighborhood and let O ⊂ TΣ be open. Suppose w ∈ O has finite future proper duration in Md and its endpoint is reached on a regular geodesic arc in a C2 extension. Then some seed w′ ∈ O first runs out of Pd at one of its noncorner branches. The new seed need not have a regular exit in that extension.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.1
candidates.name: A finite tidal observation
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.1 (A finite tidal observation).
candidates.statement: Let d ∈ Uϵ, and let w ∈ TΣ be a seed whose future unit timelike geodesic has a noncorner branch as its first runout from the comparison development Pd. Suppose its curvature is bounded in the parallel positive metric up to that runout. For every integer m ≥ 10, every η > 0, and every J > 0, there are smooth complete vacuum data dT ∈ D and seeds wT → w, for arbitrarily large finite T, such that pm(dT − d) −→ 0, and the unit geodesic of wT in the full MGHD of dT has a finite point with tangent UT and a unit spacelike vector XT ⊥ UT for which | |Riem(gdT )(UT , XT , UT , XT ) | | > J. In particular pm(dT − d) < η for sufficiently large T, and the data may be required to remain in any prescribed relatively open neighborhood of d.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.4
candidates.name: Deep comparison
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.4 (Deep comparison).
candidates.statement: Fix a mixed Sobolev comparison order k ≥ 10. For every sufficiently small fixed δ2 > 0, one may fix ε0 > 0 and then ν0 > 0 sufficiently small as follows. Suppose the exact reduced-equation Cauchy jets on s = 0 satisfy the vacuum constraints and wave-map gauge, agree with g for v < (1 − ν0)T, and differ from the jets of g + hp by at most e−7κT/2 in Hk+1 × Hk (dx dθ). (9.9) Then these data have an exact vacuum development g′ on (P1), with normalized error F = g′ −g−hp bounded in the through-k mixed energies by Ce(κ+δ2)T ( e−7κT/2 + AT λ−M1 p + A2 T λP∗ p ) . (P7) The conclusion holds when this bound has a fixed exponential margin below AT and the required base packet norms are sufficiently exponentially small. The same estimate, with fixed buffers, controls normalized C2 error.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.6
candidates.name: Backward escape and flow bounds
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.6 (Backward escape and flow bounds).
candidates.statement: The null rays launched by dv on a sufficiently small fixed entry patch, followed towards the past, return to the original initial end. For every prescribed α > 0, after choosing a sufficiently large fixed radius and then taking T sufficiently large, all their arrival points satisfy (1 − α)tT < |z − z∗| < (1 + α)tT , z∗ = Ce(tT ). (E1) Their entry crossing is unique and transverse within the computing region, with separation from the entry level outside a uniform collar. All fixed jets of the phase-space flow on all subsegments, including launch-center derivatives, have bounds eo(T). Tensor parallel transport has bounded norm and inverse along these rays. The assertions hold with short past and future launch margins, including passage through the deeper inner exit.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.7
candidates.name: Exterior beam approximation
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.7 (Exterior beam approximation).
candidates.statement: For every fixed base-order buffer Nb, every prescribed inverse accuracy M1, and sufficiently high finite phase and amplitude orders, there is a real exterior perturbation hB such that ∥hB ∥CNb ≤ AT λNb+3/2 p eo(T) , reduced-wave and gauge residuals ≤ eo(T) ( AT λ−M1 p + A2 T λP0 p ) , P0 = 2Nb + 7, (E2) after enlarging Nb for the required trace and derivative buffers. Its jets match those of hp at S with linear error AT λ−M1 p eo(T). The positive exponent P0 depends only on the base orders, not on later formal accuracy. On the original initial slice its support lies in (E1), up to arbitrarily thin tube margins.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.8
candidates.name: Protected exterior correction
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.8 (Protected exterior correction).
candidates.statement: Fix an integer s ≥ 3. Suppose dB = (δ + aB, bB) are smooth data on R3, the metric is positive, and all derivatives of aB, bB have symbol orders −1, −2, respectively. Suppose a smooth compact source ϕ, supported in {|y′| ≥ 1}, agrees with Φ(dB) there. If ∥aB∥Hs+2 1 + ∥bB∥Hs+1 2 + ∥ϕ∥Hs 4 is sufficiently small, there is a smooth correction vc supported in {|y′| ≥ 1} such that Φ(dB + vc) = 0 there, ∥vc∥Xs ≤ Cs∥ϕ∥Hs 4 . The correction is smooth across the support boundary, preserves positivity, and satisfies symbol bounds at every order. There is no higher-order smallness assumption and no condition on the artificial interior defect. No moment condition is imposed on ϕ; the correction may have a noncompact tail changing the asymptotic coefficients.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.9
candidates.name: Exterior transfer with exact early agreement
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.9 (Exterior transfer with exact early agreement).
candidates.statement: For any prescribed small δ3 > 0, the localization parameters and far threshold can be chosen so that the exact ordinary wave-map solution exists on this finite exterior domain and its error from g + hB, in the required fixed mixed norms, is bounded by Ceδ3T ( AT λ−M1 p + A2 T λP0 p ) . (E3) It is exactly g on the earlier needed compact-in-radius region up to tT − α′T, where α′ > 0 can be prescribed sufficiently small. In particular, with the choices below, its entry jets agree exactly with g for v < (1 − ν0)T and otherwise meet (9.9).

candidates.label: Proposition 9.10
candidates.name: Full-bridge Cauchy attachment
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.10 (Full-bridge Cauchy attachment).
candidates.statement: For sufficiently large finite T, the exact data dT have a smooth globally hyperbolic vacuum development containing the entire initial bridge and the finite observation from Lemma 9.5. Its adaptive backward geodesic reaches Σ with a seed wT → w. The development embeds openly in the full MGHD of dT , retaining the entire constraint-correction tail on Σ.

candidates.label: Proposition A.6
candidates.name: Far energy reduction
candidates.heading: Proposition A.6 (Far energy reduction).
candidates.statement: Assume that each equation has the splitting (A.16), and that its correction, raw, remainder, and mixed budgets satisfy, in the triangular order specified below, bounds of the form oR0→∞(1)(F + Sa) + C ∑ prior Fprior + C(R0)KR + Cfix(ein + N1+c1 ) (A.19) for fixed c1 > 0. Assume also that the corrections have initial weighted energy and averaged starting- annulus costs bounded by the initial and overlap terms in (A.19); the annular norm is the compact weighted L2 norm. Then the two energy multipliers give F ≤ o(1)(F + Sa) + C(R0)KR + Cfix(ein + N1+c2 ) (A.20) (with c2 > 0, allowing analogous small input bootstrap errors). It suffices also to take tunably small uniform coefficients on F in this argument. A convenient prior order for linear terms is: level P before the h hierarchies, within a level lower total orders first, more lab times first at fixed total order, and then fewer S’s first. Small radius gains and perturbative nonlinear effects may cross this order. Norms aggregated at equal indices are treated together.

candidates.label: Proposition B.1
candidates.name: Complete far-source estimate
candidates.heading: Proposition B.1 (Complete far-source estimate).
candidates.statement: For each commuted equation on such a finite slab, the sum of its budgets (A.17), together with its mixed charges (A.18), is bounded, for some fixed c1 > 0, by oR0→∞(1)(F + Sa) + C ∑ prior Fprior + C(R0)KR + Cfix(ein + N1+c1 ). (B.6) The finite prior order is: level P before the two h hierarchies; within each level lower total order first, then more laboratory times at equal total order, then fewer dilations S. Equal-index norms are aggregated. The constants on prior far quantities are independent of both matching radii. Small radial gains and nonlinear bootstrap products may cross this order. After fixed finite hierarchical weighting, Proposition A.6 therefore gives, for some c2 > 0, F ≤ oR0→∞(1)(F + Sa) + C(R0)KR + Cfix(ein + N1+c2 ). (B.7) The initial and starting-annulus correction costs satisfy the same bound. In particular the pure acceleration defect on the starting annulus has its direct small radial coefficient on Sa.

candidates.label: Corollary B.3
candidates.name: Global exterior estimates from the base neighborhood
candidates.heading: Corollary B.3 (Global exterior estimates from the base neighborhood).
candidates.statement: There is a neighborhood specified solely by sufficiently small p10 difference from the Kerr bridge such that the two reduced computing-cylinder evolutions are global and smooth. They obey Equations (5.7), (5.16) and (5.17) and Proposition 5.5 and (B.7), with arbitrarily small total base bounds after the neighborhood is sufficiently shrunk. The higher smooth norms on growing cylinders have the subexponential bounds of Proposition 5.6; their constants may depend on the fixed smooth datum and the order. No smallness of those higher initial norms is required.

candidates.label: Proposition D.1
candidates.name: Exact correction outside a protected ball
candidates.heading: Proposition D.1 (Exact correction outside a protected ball).
candidates.statement: Fix an integer s ≥ 3. There are constants ϵs, Cs > 0 with the following property. Let dB = (δ + aB, bB) be smooth metric and second fundamental form data on R3, with δ + aB positive definite and, for every multi-index α, |∂α aB(y)| ≤ Cα⟨y⟩−1−|α| , |∂α bB(y)| ≤ Cα⟨y⟩−2−|α| . Let ϕ be a smooth compactly supported scalar/covector pair such that supp ϕ ⊂ {|y| ≥ 1}, Φ(dB) = ϕ on |y| ≥ 1. Define the two base sizes βs = ∥aB∥Hs+2 1 + ∥bB∥Hs+1 2 , ηs = ∥ϕ∥Y s . If βs + ηs < ϵs, there is a smooth tensor pair vc = (qc, pc) such that supp vc ⊂ {|y| ≥ 1}, Φ(dB + vc) = 0 on |y| ≥ 1, ∥vc∥Xs ≤ Csηs. The corrected metric remains positive definite. The correction is smooth across |y| = 1 and satisfies symbol bounds of metric weight one and second fundamental form weight two at every order. No smallness is required of these higher bounds. No moment condition is imposed on ϕ, and the correction need not be compactly supported; its tail may change the asymptotic charges. No constraint equation is asserted for the artificially supplied datum on |y| < 1.

manuscripts.title: A two-dimensional area law from a global spectral gap

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.name: Area law
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1 (Area law).
candidates.statement: For every q, R, J as above and every ∆ > 0, there is a finite constant C = C(q, R, J, ∆) with the following property. Suppose that Λ is a finite induced square-lattice domain and that the Hamiltonian (1.1) has a unique normalized ground vector Ω, up to phase, with ground energy E0, and satisfies H − E0 id ≥ ∆ (︁ id −|Ω⟩⟨Ω| )︁ . Then for every A ⊆ Λ, SΩ(A) ≤ C |∂ΛA|. (1.2) The same constant applies to all such domains, sets, and Hamiltonians.

candidates.label: Corollary 1.2
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.2.
candidates.statement: The conclusion of Theorem 1.1 holds for every subset of a finite rectangular square lattice with bounded on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions and a unique ground state separated by a fixed global gap. For every domain covered by that theorem it also implies SΩ(A) ≤ 4C|∂inA|, SΩ(A) ≤ 2C|ZA|.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.3
candidates.name: Initial safe-box estimate
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.3 (Initial safe-box estimate).
candidates.statement: There are constants C < ∞ and e0 ∈ (0, 1), depending only on q, R, J, ∆, such that Fbox(r) ≤ Cr1+e0 (r ≥ 1). (3.21)

candidates.label: Proposition 4.3
candidates.name: Positive replacement of the Hamiltonian
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.3 (Positive replacement of the Hamiltonian).
candidates.statement: Suppose HΩ = E0Ω, ∥Ω∥ = 1, and H − E0I ≥ ∆(I − PΩ), PΩ = |Ω⟩⟨Ω|. For each integer p ≥ 1 and α = p/(p + 1), there are operators ki, indexed by the original supports and retaining their anchors, and a constant c∗ > 0 such that 0 ≤ ki ≤ I, kiΩ = 0, HF := ∑︂ i∈I ki ≥ c−1 ∗ (H − E0I) ≥ g(I − PΩ), g := ∆/c∗. (4.8) Thus HF has the unique ground vector Ω, ground energy zero, and gap at least g. Furthermore, ki,l := Ei,l(ki) ∈ [0, I], ∥ki − ki,l∥ ≤ Ce−clα (l ∈ Z≥0). (4.9) Each ki is supported in the connected component containing ai.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.5
candidates.name: Truncation near a finite set
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.5 (Truncation near a finite set).
candidates.statement: Use Proposition 4.3 with p = 1, so α = 1/2. Fix C0 > 0. There is a constant C1, depending only on q, R, J, ∆, C0, with the following property for every real n ≥ 2 and every nonempty S0 ⊆ Λ with |S0| ≤ C0n2. Put r0 = ⌈C1(log n)2⌉. If d0 i := dΛ(ai, S0) < ∞, define ri = max{r0, ⌊d0 i /2⌋}, ˜︁ hi = ki,ri , ˜︁ Xi = Nri (ai). (4.16) If d0 i = ∞, set ˜︁ hi = ki and designate its anchor’s entire component as ˜︁ Xi. Then ˜︁ H = ∑︁ i ˜︁ hi is a sum of positive contractions and ∥ ˜︁ H − HF ∥ ≤ ϵn, ϵn := min{n−1000 , g/4}. (4.17) 22 Its ground energy ˜︁ E0 lies in [0, ϵn], its ground vector ˜︁ Ω is unique, and its gap is at least g/2. After a choice of phase, ∥˜︁ Ω − Ω∥ ≤ 2 √︂ ϵn/g, 1 2 ⃦ ⃦|˜︁ Ω⟩⟨˜︁ Ω| − PΩ ⃦ ⃦ 1 ≤ √︂ 2ϵn/g. (4.18) For a set X ⊆ S0, let bX = |∂ΛX| and let CX be the labels whose designated supports ˜︁ Xi meet both X and Λ \ X. Every such support has radius exactly r0, and |CX| ≤ CbX(r0 + 1)2 , log di ≤ C(r0 + 1)2 (i ∈ CX), di := q| ˜︁ Xi| . (4.19) Consequently the cut parameter BX := 1 + ∑︂ i∈CX log2 (edi) ≤ C(1 + bX)(r0 + 1)6 . (4.20) In particular, bX ≤ C2nD and D ≥ 1 imply BX ≤ CnD(log n)12, with the constant also depending on C2.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.4
candidates.name: Entropy and energy transport
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.4 (Entropy and energy transport).

candidates.statement: Consider a family of distributed constructions indexed by L ≥ 2 with the following uniform properties. 1. The number of parties and gates is uniformly polynomial. manuscripts.title: Exact quantum factoring over a fixed finite gate set

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: There is a polynomial-time uniform family of polynomial-size quantum circuits that outputs the complete prime factorization of every input integer N ≥ 2 with probability one. The number of gates and qubits is bounded by a fixed polynomial in the bit length of N. One fixed finite gate set suffices: NOT, CNOT, Toffoli, Hadamard, diag(1, i), their inverses, and their singly controlled versions.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.1
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.1.
candidates.statement: Let 2 ≤ m < B and let a be a unit modulo m, of order r. There is a uniform quantum trial of worst-case cost polynomial in n that returns either no candidate or an integer d satisfying 1 ≤ d < B and r | d. Moreover, Pr(d = r) = φ(r)λ(r), λ(d) = 2−⌈log2 d⌉−10 . The trial uses only the fixed finite gate set specified above and does not require r or any factorization as input.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.1
candidates.name: A process with verifiable transition probabilities
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.1 (A process with verifiable transition probabilities).
candidates.statement: There is a uniformly polynomial-time process, using the order trial of Proposition 3.1, with the following properties. 1. It either aborts or generates D. A deterministic polynomial-time verifier accepts exactly these complete data. The process’s classical controller makes at most L transitions, and completed runs are padded to exactly L by constant-output dummy transitions. Each transition output has a fixed W-bit encoding. 2. Given D and the recorded classical input of a transition, one can compute a good-output predicate, one canonical good encoding, and the exact probability s that an ordinary execution of that transition has a good output. The probability s is dyadic, has polynomial bit length, and obeys s ≥ 1 − 2−2n . For a dummy transition, its constant output is good and canonical, and s = 1. 3. Every evolution whose transition outputs are all good completes the tasks and generates D without aborting or reaching a resource cap. This assertion also holds when good outputs are supplied directly. The work is polynomially bounded on arbitrary output sequences as well, with malformed outputs causing an abort. Only the transition output is included in its W-bit encoding. Internal order-trial registers and recorded computational history are separate workspace and may be retained.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.2
candidates.name: Known probability from deferred filters
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.2 (Known probability from deferred filters).
candidates.statement: The implemented preparation just described has success probability exactly p∗ = (1 − 2−n )n10 . (27) Every successful branch outputs the correct prime factorization of N. The preparation has polyno- mial worst-case time and workspace, and p∗ > 1/2 is an initially known dyadic with polynomial bit length.

candidates.name: Finite-index extension correspondence
candidates.heading: Corollary 9.3 (Finite-index extension correspondence).
candidates.statement: Let V be a simple unitary strongly rational VOA. Up to isomorphism over the embedded base, U ↦→ AU gives a one-to-one correspondence between the following classes: (1) normalized CFT-type unitary VOA extensions V ↪→ U whose underlying V -module is grading- restricted and of finite length; (2) normalized irreducible local conformal-net extensions of AV of finite index. The VOA class may equivalently be described by simple CFT-type algebraic extensions with the same conformal vector and finite-length underlying V -module, equipped with their unique unitary structure extending that of V . Let P be the normalized haploid commutative C∗-Frobenius algebra of U in Repu (V ), and let Θ be its transport to Repf (AV ) under the base equivalence. The Q-system extension BΘ equals AU as a conformal net on HU . Moreover, AU is completely rational and FU CWX ◦ FVOA = FCN ◦ ˜︁ FV CWX as braided unitary tensor functors with Gui’s tensorators. Here ˜︁ FV CWX transports unitary local (dyslectic) P-modules to local Θ-modules, and FVOA and FCN are the canonical equivalences from these categories to Repu (U) and Repf (AU ), respectively. In particular, FU CWX is a braided unitary tensor equivalence onto all finite-index sectors of AU .

More explicitly, put M = Lω(Λ) and N = Lν(Π), and let θ : pMn(M)p −→ qMm(N)q be a specified isomorphism, where the unnormalized traces of p and q are t and s. After choosing distinct germ orbits and allowing zero fibres, all bounded bi- module maps are (1.5) HomM–N ( ⨁ d H(d, σd), ⨁ d H(d, τd) ) = ⨁ d HomCd,α(σd, τd). A correspondence K = ⨁ d H(d, σd) has dimensions dimM K = ∑ d dimC(σd)[Λ : Bd], dim KN = ∑ d dimC(σd)[Γ : Ad]. Both are positive integers when K ̸= 0. candidates.statement: There is an absolute constant C < ∞ such that, for every complex Hilbert space K, every unital von Neumann algebra P ⊂ B(K), every Y ∈ B(K), every integer h ≥ 1, and every X ∈ Mh(P), ∥[Y(h) , X]∥ ≤ C gP(Y) ∥X∥. (1) Here Mh(P) acts naturally on Kh, and [T, U] = TU − UT.

candidates.heading: Theorem 2.5 (Kirchberg’s similarity–derivation equivalence).
candidates.statement: For a unital C∗-algebra A, the follow- ing properties are equivalent. 1.
